provenance.what: FEHE sizing, cost and net benefit of heat integration

method:
------
1. LMTD of counter-current flow. A shell-and-tube unit with one shell pass and an even number of tube passes
   (1-2 shell) needs the correction factor F (Bowman, Mueller and Nagle 1940 form, as given in Towler and Sinnott
   2013, Sec. 19.6). With a temperature cross (cold outlet above hot outlet, as in the AmCraX FEHE) one 1-2 shell
   is infeasible; the smallest number N of 1-2 shells in series with F >= F_MIN (0.75, textbook rule) is used.
   A pure counter-current unit (F = 1) is also reported. When the caller passes a segmented UA (from the H-T
   curves, ``amcrax.heat_integration.analyse``), the area uses that UA instead of Q / LMTD, divided by F.
2. Area A = UA / (U F). U is NOT computed here: three cases from typical-range tables (U_CASES, below).
3. Cost (CORRELATIONS): Turton et al. (2018) module costing (purchased cost Cp0 at CEPCI 397, pressure factor,
   material factor, bare-module factor) as the central correlation; Towler and Sinnott (2013) U-tube
   correlation (CEPCI 532.9, Jan 2010) with the Hand installation factor 3.5 as a cross-check. Escalated to the
   2024 cost year of the reference CAPEX by CEPCI. The central target 797.9 is the 2023 annual value used as a proxy
   for 2024; 720.2 (printed by Kum 2026 as a 2024 index) cannot be a 2024 annual index and is a sensitivity only. An area above the correlation range is split into equal parallel units; below the range the cost
   is evaluated at the lower bound (flagged).
4. TCI-equivalent = installed (bare-module) cost x the reference-scenario indirect factor
   (1 + OSBL)(1 + engineering + contingency), i.e. the same factor as every item of
   amcrax.economics.reference.reference_capex. Turton's bare-module cost already contains some indirect costs,
   so this is conservative (it counts against heat integration).
5. Annualised cost: capital charge (reference CRF) + maintenance + insurance + plant overhead on maintenance,
   with G&A, exactly as the fixed-opex formula of amcrax.economics.singapore.evaluate.

All values carry a source label; typical-range values are labelled as such.

H3-d.proposed_verdict: INCONCLUSIVE (energy half SUPPORTED; cost half threshold-dependent: sourced U straddles the break-even U)
assumptions: U typical-range cases (VDI Heat Atlas C3; central derived)
Turton 2018 module costing, SS/SS, 19.5 barg, CEPCI 797.9
TCI-equivalent = bare module x 1.4336 (reference indirect factor, conservative)
fuel saving on the unified reference basis (first-law deficit, supplementary NH3 at 450 USD/t)
reference CAPEX does not change between HI on and off; exchanger treated as incremental
H3-d.uncertainty: U 10-500 W/(m2 K), NH3 300-1000 USD/t, CRF 0.094-0.199, CEPCI 720-800, material CS/CS to SS/SS, Towler correlation, F=1 vs multi-shell
H3-d.envelope: 20 bar, 499-625 degC reactor, FEHE hot-end approach 20-200 K (python), U >= break-even U

threshold.note: break-even U (conservative multi-shell 1-2 design, SS/SS, TCI factor 1.4336) is 7.7-11.3 W/(m2 K); it lies inside the 1-bar typical range and far below the high-pressure range. No sourced value at 20 bar: a 20 bar gas is expected above the 1-bar range, but that is an engineering expectation, not a sourced number.

H3-d.reason: Energy (the H3-d claim): heat integration lowers the first-law heat deficit by 44 % and total external heating by 21 % in Aspen (baseline 600 degC), and the fuel saving is positive in every catalyst case and at every FEHE approach 20-200 K (python); it is a computed result, not a built-in assumption (the 50 K approach is an assumption, varied). Cost (reported for H3-K and the essay): the 0.214 USD/kg saving survives the exchanger cost at every U case (net 0.067-0.095 USD/kg, conservative design; 0.165-0.184 with one counter-current unit), but turns negative in adverse corners listed in net_benefit_negative_in. The cost half depends on an overall heat-transfer coefficient with no source at 20 bar: the break-even U (7.7-11.3 W/(m2 K)) lies inside the only sourced (1 bar) typical range 5-35, so the cost half is threshold-dependent (INCONCLUSIVE). Break-even CRF (solved): 0.186 / 0.223 / 0.244 at U low / central / high (reference CRF 0.110).
